sales_notes:
Summary: large fintech, strong need for private VPC deployment to meet regulator expectations. Primary ask is audit logging & SIEM integration. GRC lead = Ana Lopez. Key quote: "Logs must be immutable and searchable for 7 years; we cannot preserve raw PII in the logs."

Audit logging specific requirements (from call):
- SIEM export targets: Splunk HEC preferred, Datadog Logs intake secondary; also ability to drop raw log bundles to S3 for long-term archive (encrypted).
- Schema: JSON line records with strict fields: timestamp (ISO8601), request_id, route, model_name, model_version, truncated_input_hash, output_token_summary, token_count, latency_ms, customer_tenant_id, user_role, api_key_id (masked), event_type (request/response/admin), error_code, storage_ref (S3 path for full encrypted blob). Must support custom attributes for their internal correlation ids (trace_id, case_id).
- PII/redaction: cannot include full prompt text for regulated flows. They want a hashed/truncated input reference plus option to retain full encrypted payload in customer-owned S3 with KMS key. Redwood must provide ability to disable raw payload logging for selected routes.
- Retention: operational logs (debug/ops) = 12 months; audit/security logs = 7 years immutable (WORM); metadata indices (searchable fields) = 3 years. Need S3 lifecycle rules + Glacier tiering examples in SOW.
- Access logs: admin console access, API key rotations, onboarding actions must be logged to a separate admin audit stream with MFA result and actor identity. Read-only access for compliance team; role-based ACLs for logs.
- Integrity & immutability: support for object lock / WORM on S3; signed digests for log bundles; exportable chain-of-custody reports for auditors.
- KMS: customer-managed KMS required for long-term archives; prefer AWS KMS+HSM. Need key rotation policy, ability to bring-your-own-key (BYOK), and documented key-access audit trail.
- SIEM ingestion: 1) push via HTTPS HEC (TLS mutual auth) 2) optional syslog/collector support 3) S3 export with event batching. Expect throughput: peak 2k events/sec during trading windows; needs backpressure/fallback plan.
- Alerting: baseline suspicious activity rules (excessive token usage, rapid key failures) and webhook notifications to their SOAR.
customer_risks_notes: High: regulator-driven retention + immutability. If Redwood cannot provide BYOK + WORM + redaction controls, procurement will favor incumbent or build-in house. Also cost sensitivity if retention increases storage spend - wants clear lifecycle/archival pricing.
